name: CRAG: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2401.15884 (cs.CL; v1 Jan 29 2024, v3 Oct 7 2024). No peer-reviewed venue: the paper was submitted to ICLR 2025 (OpenReview id JnWJbrnaUE) but is recorded there as an ICLR 2025 Conference Withdrawn Submission, so the canonical/stable venue remains arXiv 2401.15884.
authors_affiliation: Shi-Qi Yan (National Engineering Research Center of Speech and Language Information Processing, University of Science and Technology of China, USTC, Hefei, China), Jia-Chen Gu (Dept. of Computer Science, University of California, Los Angeles / UCLA; equal contribution), Yun Zhu (Google DeepMind), Zhen-Hua Ling (USTC). Lead authors Shi-Qi Yan and Jia-Chen Gu (equal contribution); primary affiliations USTC and UCLA, with Google DeepMind.
code_url: https://github.com/HuskyInSalt/CRAG (official; releases inference of CRAG/Self-CRAG, retrieval-evaluator fine-tuning, evaluator weights and training data; ~460 GitHub stars, last updated Oct 2024).
maintained_repo_url: N/A (the official repo HuskyInSalt/CRAG is a frozen artifact repository, not a continuously-maintained leaderboard/paper-list).
task_domain: QA / knowledge-intensive generation (open-domain RAG). Tasks span short-form entity QA (PopQA), long-form generation (Biography), true-or-false fact verification (PubHealth), and multiple-choice reasoning (Arc-Challenge). Not an agent/tool-use/planning system; it is a corrective RAG inference framework.
problem_setting: Offline, single-turn, single-agent retrieval-augmented generation with a frozen generator LLM. The core problem is robustness of generation when retrieval 'goes wrong', i.e. when retrieved documents from a static, limited corpus are irrelevant or misleading and degrade the answer. CRAG is plug-and-play at inference and is coupled to standard RAG and Self-RAG. Supervision used: a separate lightweight retrieval evaluator (T5-large) is fine-tuned offline using relevance signals derived from datasets (e.g. PopQA's golden subject Wikipedia title) before deployment; the generator itself is not retrained. At test time the same Contriever retrieval results provided by Self-RAG are reused for comparability, plus an external web-search fallback (Google Search via the serper.dev API).
what_is_retrieved: Documents/passages (text). From the static corpus: top-k retrieved passages (Wikipedia-style, via Contriever). From the web-search fallback: web pages (Wikipedia preferred) returned by a commercial Google Search API, transcribed and refined into knowledge strips.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID, but predominantly STATIC: the primary source is a static external corpus (Wikipedia passages via Contriever); when retrieval is judged Incorrect/Ambiguous, large-scale live web search (Google/serper.dev) is added as a corrective external source. No agent-written growing/episodic memory; the web search is an external static-world query, not a memory the system accumulates.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k retrieval at the corpus level (the same top-k passages from Self-RAG/Contriever are used), but CRAG layers a precision-driven refinement on top: a decompose-then-recompose step filters retrieved passages down to a variable-size set of relevant 'knowledge strips', so the injected context is precision-driven rather than a fixed-size ranking. The objective is robustness/precision of injected knowledge, not minimal-set completeness over multiple tools/demos.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based-reasoning system). Loosely: Retrieve yes (corpus + web), Reuse yes (knowledge strips injected as context); no Revise/Retain of cases. [Retrieve, Reuse]
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as corrective retrieval-augmented generation / self-correction for RAG and does not cite or invoke case-based reasoning (Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner).
retrieval_unit: Document/passage as the retrieval unit, then a finer 'knowledge strip' as the refined unit. Each retrieved passage is segmented into internal strips (a strip is one or a few sentences, an independent piece of information); strips are scored, filtered and recomposed. So the effective injected unit is a sentence-level knowledge strip, derived from document-level retrieval.
index_source: Static corpus constructed offline (Wikipedia passages, the same Contriever-retrieved results provided by Self-RAG) plus a live external web index queried at test time (Google Search / serper.dev). No online-induced growing store; the corpus is frozen and the retrieval evaluator is fine-tuned offline.
index_structure_topology: Flat. The static corpus is a flat passage index queried by a dense retriever (Contriever); the web search returns a flat list of URLs/pages. No graph, hierarchy, or clustering of the index.
retriever_type: For the static corpus: dense retriever (Contriever, off-the-shelf, inherited from Self-RAG). For the fallback: a commercial web search engine (Google Search API via serper.dev) acting as an external retriever. CRAG itself does not introduce a new trained retriever; its novel learned component is the retrieval EVALUATOR (a fine-tuned T5-large), not the retriever. Hybrid (dense corpus retriever + web search engine).
retriever_learning_signal: The underlying corpus retriever (Contriever) is off-the-shelf (none / pretrained). CRAG's distinctive learned signal is for the lightweight retrieval EVALUATOR: T5-large (0.77B) is fine-tuned on relevance labels per (question, passage) pair, where positive relevance signals are derived from dataset metadata (e.g. PopQA's golden subject Wikipedia title used to identify high-quality passages) and negative samples are drawn from other retrieved/random passages. This is supervised relevance classification (LM-feedback-style relevance labels), not RL or contrastive interactive preference; the web search trigger is then threshold-based on the evaluator score.
query_construction: Two-stage. For corpus retrieval, the raw input query is used (the same retrieval results as Self-RAG are reused). For the web-search fallback, the input is rewritten by ChatGPT into a keyword-style search query (intent/keyword extraction) to mimic typical search-engine usage.
query_granularity: Task-level / one retrieval per query (t=0) for the corpus. The web-search query is also formed once per input (after rewriting). No per-step or trajectory-level re-querying; it is single-shot with a conditional corrective branch.
when_to_retrieve: Adaptive/active in a single corrective pass: corpus retrieval happens once per query, then a learned retrieval evaluator decides (Correct / Incorrect / Ambiguous) whether to refine the retrieved docs, discard-and-web-search, or combine both. So the corrective web-search retrieval is uncertainty/confidence-triggered (one-shot base retrieval + confidence-gated corrective retrieval), not iterative looping.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Learned relevance-evaluator confidence with two thresholds. The fine-tuned T5-large evaluator produces a relevance/confidence score per retrieved document; an upper and a lower threshold map scores to three actions: Correct (at least one doc above the upper threshold), Incorrect (all docs below the lower threshold -> trigger web search), and Ambiguous (in between -> combine refined corpus knowledge and web knowledge). The web-search corrective action is thus gated by this confidence signal, not by a fixed schedule or token-level confidence of the generator.
reranking: No explicit cross-encoder reranking of the document list. Instead, the retrieval evaluator scores each document/strip for relevance and these scores (i) trigger actions and (ii) drive knowledge-strip filtering. The scoring-then-filtering of strips functions as a relevance-based selection rather than a classic listwise reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: Decompose-then-recompose knowledge refinement: retrieved documents are segmented into knowledge strips (one-to-few sentences), each strip is scored by the retrieval evaluator, irrelevant strips are filtered out, and relevant strips are recomposed (concatenated in order) into 'internal knowledge'. The same refinement is applied to transcribed web pages to form 'external knowledge'. This is distractor filtering + decompose-then-recompose distillation, central to CRAG.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill descriptions; the system retrieves text documents/web pages, not tool APIs).
index_content_separation: N/A / No explicit lightweight-index-then-content separation. Documents are retrieved and then refined into strips; there is no progressive-disclosure SOP-index-then-content design.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Partially relevant: the corpus index is static, but a live web-search integration via a commercial Google Search API (serper.dev) provides a dynamic external knowledge source at query time. Integration protocol is a REST web-search API (URL retrieval + page transcription), not MCP/RapidAPI/function-calling, and there is no tool CRUD auto-sync.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the refined knowledge (internal corpus knowledge and/or external web knowledge) is concatenated and prepended to the query as context for the frozen generator LLM (standard RAG or Self-RAG generation). No training-signal injection into the generator; retrieval purely conditions generation. The retrieval evaluator additionally acts as a control/router determining which knowledge is assembled.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-(evaluate/correct)-then-generate, single-pass. There is no multi-step planner, MCTS, or tree search. The 'planning' is a fixed corrective decision tree: retrieve from corpus -> evaluate relevance -> branch into {refine, web-search, combine} -> generate. When coupled with Self-RAG, Self-RAG's own reflection-token generation runs on top of the CRAG-corrected context.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer. Retrieval/correction occurs once before the answer is generated; it is not interleaved per CoT step, per sentence/token, or per tool-call. (When wrapped around Self-RAG, Self-RAG may still do segment-level reflection, but CRAG's correction itself is per-query/per-answer.)
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no CBR case adaptation). The closest analogue is the decompose-then-recompose refinement that adapts raw retrieved documents into filtered knowledge strips, but this is content filtering, not case revision.
retrieved_item_representation: Free-text knowledge: refined 'knowledge strips' (relevant sentence-level fragments concatenated in order) drawn from corpus passages (internal knowledge) and/or transcribed web pages (external knowledge). Raw-text, not distilled strategies, programs, or latent tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw factual text at sentence/strip granularity (filtered passage fragments). Not a distilled strategy, workflow, skill, or hint; it is concrete evidence text selected for relevance.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Core contribution. (1) A learned lightweight retrieval evaluator (relevance scorer) that detects when retrieval is wrong; (2) confidence-thresholded corrective actions {Correct, Incorrect, Ambiguous}, with the Ambiguous action explicitly added to reduce dependence on evaluator accuracy; (3) web-search fallback to replace irrelevant corpus knowledge; (4) decompose-then-recompose strip filtering to remove irrelevant/distractor content within retrieved documents. Together these guard against irrelevant/incorrect retrieved context.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory; static corpus + live web search only).
write_back: False. The system does not store new experiences, cases, or knowledge back into any memory store; web-search results are used transiently for the current query and not persisted.
online_growth: No. The retrievable corpus and the fine-tuned evaluator are frozen after offline setup; nothing grows during deployment (web search is a transient external query, not an accumulating store).
failure_experience_usage: N/A / success-oriented. CRAG corrects per-query retrieval failures at inference (discard-and-web-search when retrieval is judged Incorrect) but does not store failed experiences/trajectories for later retrieval. During offline evaluator fine-tuning, irrelevant/negative (question, passage) pairs serve as negative training labels, but no failure experiences are retained at deployment.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored entries; nothing is mutated, merged, or pruned post-write).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially. The decision of WHICH corrective action to take is governed by a learned (fine-tuned T5-large) relevance evaluator with fixed thresholds, which is more than fixed similarity top-k routing. However, it is a supervised relevance classifier driving a hand-designed threshold/decision rule, NOT an RL/value-based sequential retrieval policy (no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, or interactive preference optimization). The underlying corpus retrieval is fixed top-k.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A / No. Single-system, single-generator setting; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing. (CRAG is, however, plug-and-play across different RAG frameworks/generators, e.g. standard RAG and Self-RAG, but it does not share an experience store across agents.)
benchmarks: PopQA (short-form entity QA), Biography / Bio (long-form generation), PubHealth / Pub (true-or-false health fact verification), Arc-Challenge / ARC (multiple-choice science QA). Four datasets total. Retrieval uses the same Contriever results provided by Self-RAG; web search via Google Search API (serper.dev).
benchmark_family: QA / knowledge-intensive generation: PopQA (open-domain short-form QA), Biography (long-form generation/factuality), PubHealth (fact verification / true-or-false), Arc-Challenge (multiple-choice reasoning QA). No web-agent, embodied, tool, code, memory, or decision-RL benchmarks.
baselines: Without retrieval: LLaMA2-7B/13B, Alpaca-7B/13B, CoVE-65B, LLaMA2-chat-13B, ChatGpt. With retrieval / standard RAG: LLaMA2-7B/13B (RAG), Alpaca-7B/13B (RAG), and the Self-RAG-instruction-tuned LLaMA2-7B as standard RAG; Ret-LLaMA2-chat-13B; cited private-data baselines Ret-ChatGPT, Ret-LLaMA-chat, and perplexity.ai. Advanced RAG: Self-RAG (Asai et al., ICLR 2024). CRAG/Self-CRAG are compared head-to-head against standard RAG and Self-RAG on the same inputs; also a ChatGPT (zero-shot / CoT / few-shot) relevance-judge baseline for evaluator quality.
key_metrics: Accuracy for PopQA, PubHealth, and Arc-Challenge; FactScore for Biography (long-form). Plus evaluator-quality accuracy (relevance-judgment accuracy on PopQA), computational overhead (TFLOPs per token, execution time per instance), and a robustness curve vs degraded retrieval performance.
headline_result: Coupled with the SelfRAG-LLaMA2-7B generator, CRAG outperformed standard RAG by +7.0% accuracy on PopQA, +14.9 FactScore on Biography, +36.6% accuracy on PubHealth, and +15.4% accuracy on Arc-Challenge; and Self-CRAG outperformed the state-of-the-art Self-RAG by +20.0% accuracy on PopQA, +36.9 FactScore on Biography, and +4.0% accuracy on Arc-Challenge when based on the original LLaMA2-hf-7B (and by +6.9 PopQA, +5.0 Bio, +2.4 PubHealth on SelfRAG-LLaMA2-7B). Main results table: Self-CRAG reaches PopQA 61.8 / Bio 86.2 / Pub 74.8 / ARC 67.2 (vs Self-RAG 54.9 / 81.2 / 72.4 / 67.3) on SelfRAG-LLaMA2-7B.
ablations: (1) Removing each action {Correct, Incorrect, Ambiguous} on PopQA: every removal drops accuracy (e.g. CRAG 54.9->53.2 w/o Correct, 54.4 w/o Incorrect, 54.0 w/o Ambiguous on LLaMA2-hf-7b; Self-CRAG 49.0 drops to 43.6/47.7/48.1), showing each action contributes, with Ambiguous reducing dependence on evaluator accuracy. (2) Removing each knowledge-utilization operation {document refinement, search-query rewriting, external-knowledge selection} on PopQA: all hurt (CRAG 54.9->49.8 w/o refinement, 51.7 w/o rewriting, 50.9 w/o selection; Self-CRAG 49.0->35.9 / 37.2 / 24.9 on LLaMA2-hf-7b). (3) Retrieval-evaluator accuracy on PopQA: T5-based evaluator 84.3% vs ChatGPT 58.0 / ChatGPT-CoT 62.4 / ChatGPT-few-shot 64.7. (4) Consistent web-search supplementation: adding web knowledge to plain RAG/Self-RAG helps only marginally (e.g. RAG 50.5->52.2 w. web), confirming gains stem from the self-correction mechanism, not merely extra web data. (5) Robustness: as retrieval quality is artificially degraded, Self-CRAG degrades more gracefully than Self-RAG.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes, partially. End-to-end task metrics (accuracy/FactScore) are reported, and the intrinsic quality of the retrieval evaluator (relevance-judgment accuracy 84.3% on PopQA) is reported separately (Table 4). However, standard IR metrics like Recall@k / nDCG of the retriever itself are not reported.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Primarily outcome metrics (final accuracy/FactScore), but process-level evaluation is included: the relevance-judgment accuracy of the retrieval evaluator (an intermediate component) and a robustness study of how generation quality tracks degraded retrieval performance.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported. The retrieval evaluator is lightweight (T5-large, 0.77B) vs Self-RAG's critic (instruction-tuned LLaMA2-7B). Computational overhead (generation-phase estimate, retrieval/data-processing excluded): RAG 26.5 TFLOPs/token & 0.363 s/instance vs CRAG 27.2 TFLOPs/token & 0.512 s; Self-RAG 26.5~132.4 TFLOPs/token & 0.741 s vs Self-CRAG 27.2~80.2 TFLOPs/token & 0.908 s. Self-CRAG's upper bound is lower because only three passages (correct/incorrect/ambiguous) are provided. The web-search fallback adds external API latency/cost not fully quantified. Conclusion: modest overhead for substantial accuracy gains.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Precision-driven / variable: the decompose-then-recompose step yields a variable number of relevant knowledge strips rather than a fixed-k passage budget; in the Self-CRAG setup the generator receives a compact three-passage representation (correct, incorrect, ambiguous content), which also lowers compute. The base corpus retrieval reuses Self-RAG's top-k passages. No explicit token-budget cap is stated; selection is reranked/filtered-then-recomposed by evaluator relevance scores.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (empirical method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing public datasets PopQA, Biography, PubHealth, Arc-Challenge; not a new benchmark). Retrieval results and eval splits are reused from Self-RAG for comparability.
builds_on: Standard RAG (Lewis et al., 2020) and Self-RAG (Asai et al., ICLR 2024) as the host frameworks; Contriever (Izacard et al., 2022) as the corpus retriever; T5-large (Raffel et al., 2020) as the retrieval evaluator backbone; web-search-augmentation lines (Piktus et al., 2021; Komeili et al., 2022); FactScore (Min et al., 2023) for long-form evaluation; LLaMA2 (Touvron et al., 2023) generators.
contrasts_with: Self-RAG (which instruction-tunes the LLM to emit reflection/critic tokens and needs a 7B critic, and degrades when the underlying LLM is not specially tuned) - CRAG argues its external lightweight evaluator is plug-and-play and does not require retraining the generator; standard RAG (which always uses raw top-k documents regardless of relevance); CoVE (chain-of-verification, no retrieval); naive web-search supplementation (shown to help only marginally without the self-correction mechanism); using ChatGPT as a relevance judge (underperforms the fine-tuned T5 evaluator).
lineage: Group B (rag_task_solving): a robust/corrective RAG method in the adaptive-RAG lineage. It sits alongside Self-RAG (self-reflective retrieval) and active-/adaptive-retrieval work, introducing a confidence-gated corrective controller (relevance evaluator -> {refine, web-search, combine}) and decompose-then-recompose refinement. A foundational 'Corrective RAG' (CRAG) reference frequently cited by later agentic/corrective RAG and graph-based RAG systems.
